item.title: BTS Beats The Rolling Stones’ Seven-Year Boxscore Record
item.description:
Here's a short, engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Upbeat music plays in the background]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music industry. I'm your host, [Name], and today we're talking about the unstoppable BTS. The K-pop sensation has been making waves on the Billboard Boxscore charts, and we're here to break it down for you."
[Sound effects: A quick music transition]
Host: "In April, BTS returned to the Top Tours chart with a bang, leading the pack for the first time in four years with a whopping $75 million in monthly earnings. But that was just the beginning. In May, they maintained their crown and leveled up, grossing a massive $127.8 million and selling 641,000 tickets over 12 shows."
[Sound effects: A brief pause for emphasis]
Host: "That's the biggest monthly gross by a group since the chart began in 2019, surpassing The Rolling Stones' $95 million record by 35%. This marks BTS' fourth month at No. 1 on Top Tours, and their biggest yet. In fact, their May earnings are the fifth biggest monthly gross in the chart's history."
[Sound effects: A quick music transition]
Host: "So, what's behind BTS' success? Well, their Arirang World Tour has been a game-changer. With a slate of shows exclusively in North America, they've been able to capitalize on higher ticket prices and bigger stadiums. The tour hit a peak in Las Vegas, with 246,000 tickets sold and $49.5 million grossed at Allegiant Stadium."
[Sound effects: A brief applause]
Host: "And the numbers keep adding up. Since the tour kicked off in April, BTS has grossed $204 million and sold 1.1 million tickets. With over 50 shows left to play, it's likely to become their biggest tour yet, surpassing their Love Yourself World Tour's $213.9 million record."
[Sound effects: A final music transition]
Host: "BTS' May shows have also pushed their career Boxscore earnings past the half-billion mark, with $503.1 million from 3.3 million tickets sold. That's a testament to their dedicated fan base and their ability to put on a show like no other. We can't wait to see what's next for this talented group."
[Music and sound effects fade out]
Host: "Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. If you want to stay up-to-date on the latest music news and trends, be sure to subscribe to our show and follow us on social media. Until next time, goodbye!"
